seo.title: Frequently asked questions
seo.description: Answers about TablePro’s apps, supported databases, paid plans, licenses, privacy and accounts.

header.title: Frequently asked questions
header.lead: Short answers, each with a link to the page that has the details.

items.question: What is TablePro?
items.answer: A native, open-source database client for Mac and Linux, with an app for iPhone and iPad, built without Electron or JDBC. It runs queries, edits data and works with schemas: <features>see all features</features>.

items.question: Is TablePro open source?
items.answer: Yes. The apps, the code for paid features included, are under the AGPLv3 in one <source>GitHub repository</source>, and a build from source still checks your plan for paid features.

items.question: How does TablePro compare with other database clients?
items.answer: Each <compare>comparison</compare> lists the differences with a checked date and its sources, including where another client may fit better.

items.question: Is TablePro free?
items.answer: Yes, with no trial or time limit: every supported engine, the AI assistant, MCP and Safe Mode are free, and the iPhone and iPad app has no in-app purchases. Pro and Team add the features on the <pricing>pricing page</pricing>.

items.question: What does a paid plan add?
items.answer: Pro adds {starterFeatures}. Team also adds {teamFeatures}: <pricingFeatures>compare the plans</pricingFeatures>.

items.question: Can I use the free app at work?
items.answer: Yes, in a company of any size, and nothing free today will become paid. The AGPL sets conditions on distributing TablePro or offering a changed version over a network, not on running it: <agpl>read the license</agpl>.

items.question: Is Pro free for students and teachers?
items.answer: Yes, for one year: sign in to <account>your account</account> with your school or university email and choose <ui>Get Pro free</ui>. It is Pro for one person, renews while the address works, and is not for an account that already paid for Pro.

more.text: Prices, billing, invoices, refunds, seats, license keys and offline use are in the <pricingFaq>questions on Pricing</pricingFaq>.

items.question: Which Macs does TablePro run on?
items.answer: The Mac app requires {macRequirement} and runs natively on Apple silicon and Intel. Get it from the <download>download page</download> or with Homebrew.

items.question: Is there a version for Windows or Linux?
items.answer: Linux, yes: <downloadLinux>TablePro for Linux</downloadLinux> is a beta for {linuxDistributions}, and for other distributions through Flatpak, with its own set of engines and features. There is no Windows version, and no release date for one.

items.question: Is there an app for iPhone and iPad?
items.answer: Yes, a free App Store app that requires {iosRequirement} and connects to {iosEngines}. It runs queries over SSH tunnels with Safe Mode and Face ID, and has no AI assistant, MCP server or saved queries: <ios>see what it does</ios>.

items.question: Which languages are the apps in?
items.answer: The Mac app is in {macLanguages}, though some screens still show English, the Linux app in {linuxLanguages}, and the iPhone and iPad app in {iosLanguages}. The website is in more languages, and the <docs>documentation</docs> is in English.

items.question: Which databases can I connect to?
items.answer: The Mac app connects to {featuredEngines} and more, and the Linux and iPhone and iPad apps to their own sets. <databases>Supported databases</databases> lists each engine’s capabilities.

items.question: Do I have to install database drivers?
items.answer: No: the Mac app comes with drivers for {bundledEngines}, and downloads the others as plugins the first time you need one, after checking their checksum and code signature. The iPhone and iPad drivers are built in.

items.question: Can I connect through SSH or TLS?
items.answer: Yes, where the engine supports them: on the Mac, SSH keys, passwords, agents and jump hosts, TLS certificate verification, and external tunnels or proxies. iPhone and iPad use SSH with a password or a private key, without jump hosts: <connections>see the connection options</connections>.

items.question: Can I bring my connections from another app?
items.answer: Yes. The Mac app imports connections, with their saved passwords, SSH tunnels and TLS settings, from {importApps}, for free.

items.question: What do the apps send to TablePro?
items.answer: Usage data without hostnames, usernames, passwords, queries or rows, on by default on Mac and Linux and opt-in on iPhone and iPad, and a check of your plan once you sign in: <securityNetwork>see everything that leaves your device</securityNetwork>.

items.question: Where are my passwords stored?
items.answer: In the Keychain on Mac, iPhone and iPad and in the desktop keyring on Linux, never on a TablePro server: <securityCredentials>see how credentials are kept</securityCredentials>.

items.question: Does the AI assistant send my data to TablePro?
items.answer: No, its requests go straight to the provider you choose, or stay on your computer with {localAiProviders}: <securityAi>see where each AI request goes</securityAi>.

items.question: What does iCloud Sync store, and where?
items.answer: Nothing until you turn it on; then the connections and settings you choose go to a private database in your own iCloud account that TablePro cannot read, with passwords only if you also turn on password sync: <securityCredentials>see what syncs</securityCredentials>.

items.question: Do I need an account?
items.answer: Not for the free app; paid features work once you sign in to the <account>TablePro account</account> of the email you bought with, by email link, passkey, Apple, GitHub or Google. Older Mac builds take a license key instead.

items.question: What is priority support?
items.answer: Emails from Team customers are answered first, within {businessDays}. The <termsSupport>terms</termsSupport> describe support for every plan.

items.question: How do I report a security problem?
items.answer: Privately, by email or a GitHub security advisory, never in a public issue: <securityReport>see how to report a vulnerability</securityReport>.
